A.explanation: A straight line through the origin would mean $f$ is proportional to $\lambda$, but $v = f\lambda$ gives $f = v/\lambda$ which decreases with $\lambda$.

B.explanation: A straight line through the origin is wrong for $f$ against $\lambda$, even though the steeper line correctly assigns the larger speed $440 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to the string.

C.explanation: Both curves show $f = v/\lambda$ decreasing as $1/\lambda$, and the string curve is above the air curve because $440 \text{ m s}^{-1} > 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

D.explanation: The curves have the correct $1/\lambda$ shape but the labels are reversed, placing the slower air wave above the faster string wave.

walkthrough: Identify the given data: wave speed in the string is $v = 440 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and sound speed in air is $v = 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
State the governing rule $v = f\lambda$, so $f = v/\lambda$ at constant $v$.
Deduce the graph shape: $f$ is inversely proportional to $\lambda$, so each plot is a rectangular hyperbola falling toward zero as $\lambda$ increases.
Compare the two media at any fixed $\lambda$: $f_{string} = 440/\lambda$ is larger than $f_{air} = 330/\lambda$, so the string curve lies above the air curve.
